frozen_truth.title: Miguel Santos — honest backend engineer behind an over-broad architecture label

authoring_metadata.source_basis: A fictional backend engineer whose resume compresses team architecture into personal language, with strong idempotency and tenant-isolation ownership, one incident, an unowned infrastructure layer, and a protected production boundary.
authoring_metadata.non_gold_reason: The world has not been calibrated with senior backend reviewers or real hiring outcomes and must not be used as an accepted benchmark.

identity.name: Miguel Santos

biography.text: Miguel is a backend engineer at a logistics software company. He grew from maintaining billing integrations into owning reliability-heavy services. He likes systems where ambiguous external outcomes are made auditable, but he is less comfortable presenting work that was genuinely collective as his own.

identity.non_evaluative_identity_note: Name, pronouns, and location are fictional context and must not influence assessment.

target_role.title: Backend Engineer

hiring_context.text: The hiring team needs a backend engineer who can reason about retries, state transitions, isolation, observability, and incident recovery while being precise about the boundary of personal ownership.

responsibilities.text: Design and maintain reliable service behavior when external calls have ambiguous outcomes.
Protect tenant data and prevent cross-tenant effects through explicit boundaries.
Collaborate on architecture without claiming decisions made by a team.
Learn from production incidents and improve detection and recovery.

why_it_matters.text: Retries and ambiguous external outcomes are central to the services Miguel actually owned.
The role requires preventing one customer's state or authorization from affecting another.
A real production incident can reveal whether the candidate reasons beyond the happy path.
The resume's word architected compresses a team decision into an individual claim.
Miguel's experience with service correctness should not be confused with ownership of cluster operations or every platform layer.

do_not_assume: A team architecture decision was Miguel's sole design.
Not owning Kubernetes or network policy means he cannot reason about backend reliability.

resume.text:
MIGUEL SANTOS
Backend Engineer | Go, Java, Postgres, Kafka, Kubernetes

ParcelGrid — Backend Engineer (2020–present)
• Architected a multi-tenant shipment and billing platform processing 18M events/day.
• Designed distributed retry and idempotency strategy for carrier and payment integrations.
• Improved duplicate-charge incidents by 80% and reduced reconciliation time.

Earlier work
• Built Java services for inventory reservation and customer notifications.
• Led on-call improvements and incident reviews across the backend group.

claims.claim_text: Architected a multi-tenant shipment and billing platform processing 18M events/day.
claims.risk_if_overread: The platform architecture was team-owned; Miguel owned important reliability components rather than the complete architecture.

claims.claim_text: Designed the distributed retry and idempotency strategy for carrier and payment integrations.
claims.risk_if_overread: The strategy covered integration state and reconciliation, not every service or queue in the platform.
The reduction followed one remediation slice and is not a guarantee of zero duplicates.

claims.claim_text: Led on-call improvements and incident reviews across the backend group.
claims.risk_if_overread: Leadership of review practice is not the same as owning infrastructure operations.

resume_limits.text: Architected is broader than the personal scope Miguel can defend; the architecture review was collaborative.
The resume omits the exact production incident and the tenant-isolation subsystem that best show his personal engineering judgment.

question.text: Can Miguel correct the architecture claim and still demonstrate substantial backend ownership?

why_it_matters.text: A fair hiring read must distinguish over-broad wording from lack of meaningful contribution.

failure_modes: Re-prosecuting the resume wording after the boundary is clear
Treating a narrower subsystem as trivial
hiring_hypotheses.uncertain_if_unresolved: The reviewer cannot tell whether the claim was a harmless compression or a pattern of ownership inflation.

question.text: Does Miguel understand how idempotency, retries, and reconciliation interact under ambiguous outcomes?

why_it_matters.text: This is the strongest role-relevant evidence of personal backend depth.

failure_modes: A solution that retries side effects without durable state
hiring_hypotheses.uncertain_if_unresolved: Backend correctness remains partly untested even if the ownership boundary is fair.

question.text: Can he explain and defend a tenant-isolation boundary without relying on platform slogans?

why_it_matters.text: The service handles shared infrastructure where authorization and data partitioning must survive retries and operational mistakes.

failure_modes: Only naming row-level security without failure analysis
Assuming tenant IDs are sufficient protection
hiring_hypotheses.uncertain_if_unresolved: Isolation may be strong in practice but not observable from the interview.

question.text: Does Miguel turn an incident into a durable system and process improvement?

why_it_matters.text: The incident is a real test of diagnosis, ownership, and follow-through.

failure_modes: Blaming a dependency without explaining recovery
Calling a dashboard an improvement without a detection or prevention change
hiring_hypotheses.uncertain_if_unresolved: Operational judgment is not sufficiently separated from resume claims.

strengths.label: Idempotent integration workflows

description.text: Miguel can reason concretely about event identity, durable state, retry classes, and reconciliation when an external outcome is ambiguous.

strengths.how_it_can_be_misread: A reviewer focused on the resume overclaim may under-credit the subsystem depth.

strengths.label: Tenant isolation

description.text: He personally designed a tenant-context boundary and negative tests for cross-tenant access in a shared service.

strengths.how_it_can_be_misread: The word multi-tenant can make the reviewer assume he owned the whole platform.

weaknesses.label: Scope communication and architecture narrative

description.text: Miguel allowed the resume to say architected and becomes defensive when the phrase is challenged, even though he can state a narrower truthful boundary.

weaknesses.how_it_can_be_misread: Defensiveness can be read as deception, or the corrected boundary can be treated as evidence that the subsystem was unimportant.

unknowns.label: Capacity planning at larger scale

why_unknown.text: The world establishes event volume but not Miguel's personal ownership of capacity forecasts or partition planning.

unknowns.fair_test: Ask how he would identify a saturation risk in the owned workflow without demanding an architecture lecture.

unknowns.label: Security operations and secrets management

why_unknown.text: Tenant isolation is evidenced, but secrets rotation and incident access processes belong partly to another team.

unknowns.fair_test: Ask for a conceptual threat or boundary, not proprietary controls.

unknowns.label: Formal people management

why_unknown.text: Miguel led review practice but has no evidence of performance management or team staffing responsibility.

unknowns.fair_test: Do not test unless the role requires it; otherwise mark not role required.

communication_effects.text: Miguel explains mechanisms clearly after the question is concrete, but a broad challenge to the resume makes him defensive for one or two turns.
He uses precise reliability vocabulary, yet will explicitly say when he does not own a layer or cannot disclose a provider detail.

answer_realizations.question_shape: Tell me about the platform you architected.
answer_realizations.answer_text: It is a multi-tenant shipment and billing platform. I led the retry and idempotency part of the design; the service decomposition was a backend-group decision.
answer_realizations.notes: A broad opener elicits a partially corrected claim.

answer_realizations.question_shape: Which architecture decisions were actually yours?
answer_realizations.answer_text: The resume says architected too broadly. The group chose the overall decomposition. I owned the operation identity, retry classification, reconciliation handoff, and tenant context in two services.
answer_realizations.notes: Candid correction followed by adjacent strength.

answer_realizations.question_shape: How did your retry strategy prevent duplicate side effects?
answer_realizations.answer_text: We persisted a stable operation identity before the external call. A transport failure could retry, but an ambiguous side effect went to reconciliation instead of being replayed blindly.

answer_realizations.question_shape: Tell me about a production failure.
answer_realizations.answer_text: A provider acknowledged after our timeout, and a migration path lost the operation identity. The retry created a second side effect. I traced the sequence, restored the state transition, and added a replay test and reconciliation state.
answer_realizations.notes: Real incident with mechanism and durable consequence.

answer_realizations.question_shape: How did you protect tenants in a shared service?
answer_realizations.answer_text: Tenant context was established at the request boundary and carried through the message. We had negative tests for replayed context and logged rejected cross-tenant attempts.

answer_realizations.question_shape: How did you manage Kubernetes capacity and network policy?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I did not own those. Platform handled upgrades, network policy, and capacity. I provided service requirements and consumed the interface.
answer_realizations.notes: An honest scope boundary, not a technical failure.

answer_realizations.question_shape: What exact provider timeout and fraud threshold did you use?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I cannot share those exact values. I can explain the state categories: known success, known failure, ambiguous outcome, retry eligibility, and reconciliation.
answer_realizations.notes: Fair abstraction after a secret request.

answer_realizations.question_shape: But were you the architect, yes or no?
answer_realizations.answer_text: No, not of the whole platform. I owned the reliability slices I described. I am happy to go deeper on those rather than relabel the team design.
answer_realizations.notes: Repeated prosecution should not create a new fact.

answer_realizations.question_shape: How do you help newer engineers?
answer_realizations.answer_text: I review onboarding pull requests twice a week and leave written examples. It is informal; I have not managed people.
answer_realizations.notes: Ordinary human detail and scope clarity.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Ask whether Miguel was the architect after he has explicitly corrected the team boundary.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: It adds no new ownership evidence and makes the candidate defend wording instead of demonstrating backend skill.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Turns a resume compression into an endless character trial.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Treat idempotency or tenant isolation ownership as ownership of the entire architecture.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: The facts explicitly separate a subsystem from team decomposition.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Either inflates the candidate unfairly or later punishes him for an interviewer-created claim.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Demand exact provider timeout, fraud, or customer identifiers to validate the incident.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: The details are protected and generic state reasoning is available.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Rewards confidentiality violations and mislabels refusal as evasiveness.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Run a Kubernetes or network-policy trivia exam after the candidate states the platform boundary.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: The world does not give him ownership or memory of those internals, and the target role is service-focused.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Converts an unowned area into a false backend weakness.

hard_invalid_moves.action: Require a yes/no exactly-once guarantee without allowing a distinction between local state and external side effects.
hard_invalid_moves.why_invalid: The relevant engineering truth is conditional idempotency plus reconciliation, not a slogan.
hard_invalid_moves.candidate_harm: Penalizes precise systems reasoning for refusing an impossible guarantee.

evidence_sufficiency.minimum_turn_shape: A good interview should establish the architecture boundary once, then obtain one owned correctness mechanism, one incident or counterfactual, and a scoped read on tenant isolation or another independent dimension.

uncertainty_map.question: Can Miguel reason about capacity and partitions beyond his service slice?
uncertainty_map.why_it_remains: The platform scale is contextual and team-owned.
uncertainty_map.fair_next_test: Ask about one saturation signal at the owned boundary.
uncertainty_map.do_not_convert_to: Do not infer weakness from not owning the whole architecture.

uncertainty_map.question: How would he coordinate a security issue crossing service and platform boundaries?
uncertainty_map.why_it_remains: The service boundary is strong, but platform security is not his area.
uncertainty_map.fair_next_test: Use a conceptual interface and escalation scenario.
uncertainty_map.do_not_convert_to: Do not demand protected controls or secrets.

uncertainty_map.question: Was architected a one-time shorthand or a recurring pattern?
uncertainty_map.why_it_remains: One corrected claim cannot establish a broader integrity pattern.
uncertainty_map.fair_next_test: Ask for another project with the same ownership precision.
uncertainty_map.do_not_convert_to: Do not treat one resume verb as a character verdict.

interviewer_failure_conditions: Continuing to prosecute the word architected after correction.
Failing to probe the adjacent subsystem because the resume claim was imperfect.
Testing platform operations as if they were personally owned.
Accepting exactly-once language without failure mechanics.
likely_traps: The resume's architecture verb is salient.
Miguel's defensive tone can bias the reviewer.
The 80% incident reduction can distract from the actual mechanism.
gold_rejection_reasons: If the world forces the candidate to answer the architecture correction in one scripted way.
If alternate questions about retries, isolation, or incidents produce inconsistent personal scope.
If the interviewer cannot distinguish unowned platform work from weak backend reasoning.
If the incident exists only to prove the candidate is strong rather than to leave meaningful uncertainty.

evidence_units.label: Current backend role

statement.text: Miguel is a backend engineer at ParcelGrid, a logistics software company with shipment and billing integrations.

ownership.boundary_text: Role context is not proof of architecture ownership.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Introduction
disclosure.allowed_summary: Backend role and logistics domain
prohibited_expansion: Do not assume every platform layer was personal.

relations.reason: The role sits in a cross-functional backend group.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Neutral grounding context.

evidence_units.label: Growth toward reliability work

statement.text: Miguel moved from maintaining integrations into reliability-heavy ownership because he enjoyed making ambiguous external outcomes auditable.

ownership.boundary_text: Motivation is not a substitute for technical evidence.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Career-history question
disclosure.allowed_summary: Why reliability work became his focus
prohibited_expansion: Do not infer seniority from motivation alone.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Ordinary context that helps the human story.

evidence_units.label: Architecture review environment

statement.text: ParcelGrid has a backend group, a platform team, and a security team; architecture decisions are reviewed in design documents, while individual engineers own specific services or reliability slices.

ownership.boundary_text: Architecture review is collective even when a person authors a proposal.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question about design ownership or collaboration
disclosure.allowed_summary: How architecture and service ownership were divided
prohibited_expansion: Do not disclose internal project names or security details.

relations.reason: The process makes sole architecture ownership unlikely.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Critical context for a fair overclaim read.

evidence_units.label: Over-broad architected resume wording

statement.text: Miguel's resume says he architected the multi-tenant shipment and billing platform, but the architecture was produced through a team design process and he did not own every subsystem.

ownership.scope: Resume narrative about the complete platform
ownership.boundary_text: The word architected is broader than Miguel's actual contribution.
ownership.owned_by: Team for platform architecture; Miguel for selected subsystems

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Resume claim is discussed
disclosure.allowed_summary: Team-owned architecture with a narrower personal subsystem
prohibited_expansion: Do not force a binary liar/not-liar interpretation.

relations.reason: The over-broad label sits above genuine owned reliability work.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: A correction point, not an automatic hiring verdict.

evidence_units.label: Team-owned architecture boundary

statement.text: The architecture was agreed by a small backend group; Miguel authored the retry and state-transition sections and implemented the idempotency and tenant-context components, but did not choose the whole service decomposition.

ownership.boundary_text: Miguel owned reliability components, not the complete architecture.
ownership.owned_by: Miguel for retry, idempotency, and tenant-context sections; team for decomposition

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Candidate is asked to separate the team architecture from personal decisions
disclosure.allowed_summary: Team architecture with personally owned reliability slices
prohibited_expansion: Do not shrink the owned slices into mere participation.

relations.reason: The boundary identifies the genuine owned subsystem.
Tenant context was one owned slice.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Once established, the interviewer should move to substance rather than revisit the label.

evidence_units.label: Platform event volume

statement.text: The platform handled approximately 18 million shipment and billing events per day during Miguel's tenure, with traffic patterns varying by carrier and customer seasonality.

ownership.boundary_text: Miguel contributed to services operating at this scale but did not own all capacity planning.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question about operating context
disclosure.allowed_summary: Approximate event volume and seasonality
prohibited_expansion: Do not use volume as a substitute for mechanism evidence.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Scale is context, not an automatic complexity score.

evidence_units.label: Idempotency and retry subsystem

statement.text: Miguel designed an integration state machine keyed by a stable operation identity, persisted the last known external outcome, separated retryable transport failures from ambiguous side effects, and sent unresolved cases to reconciliation instead of blindly retrying.

ownership.scope: Integration idempotency, retry classification, and reconciliation handoff
ownership.boundary_text: He owned this subsystem and its service-level behavior, not all platform queues or deployments.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Candidate names the owned reliability slice
disclosure.allowed_summary: Stable operation identity, retry classification, and reconciliation
prohibited_expansion: Do not ask for provider-specific secrets or internal code names.

relations.reason: The subsystem was shaped by the production incident.
Service correctness and cluster operations were adjacent but separately owned.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Strong adjacent substance that should be tested once or twice, not used to justify replaying the overclaim.

evidence_units.label: Tenant-isolation subsystem

statement.text: Miguel owned the tenant-context middleware and negative tests that prevented a request or replayed message from using another customer's authorization scope; he also added audit fields for rejected cross-tenant attempts.

ownership.scope: Tenant context propagation, authorization checks, and negative tests
ownership.boundary_text: Database administration and platform identity infrastructure were not his ownership.
ownership.owned_by: Miguel for service boundary and tests

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question about the multi-tenant claim or safety boundary
disclosure.allowed_summary: Tenant-context boundary, negative tests, and rejection audit
prohibited_expansion: Do not ask for customer identifiers or exact security controls.

relations.reason: Both are owned correctness slices in the shared architecture.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Meaningful adjacent strength, not a consolation prize.

evidence_units.label: Duplicate-charge production incident

statement.text: A carrier-payment adapter acknowledged a request after a timeout, then a retry created a second side effect because the earlier operation identity was not persisted across a migration path; Miguel traced the sequence and led the remediation.

ownership.scope: Diagnosis, state-machine remediation, and review; payment provider and migration platform were shared
ownership.boundary_text: Miguel did not control every dependency that contributed to the incident.
ownership.owned_by: Miguel for diagnosis and integration remediation; team for migration and provider boundary

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question asks for a production failure or the origin of the retry design
disclosure.allowed_summary: Timeout acknowledgment, migration path, duplicate side effect, and remediation
prohibited_expansion: Do not request provider contracts or customer billing identifiers.

relations.reason: The incident led to durable review and monitoring changes.
The incident demonstrates a subsystem, not whole-platform ownership.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Real incident evidence with a shared boundary.

evidence_units.label: Durable incident practice

statement.text: After the incident, Miguel added a replayable failure test, an explicit reconciliation queue state, and a review checklist that asks whether every external side effect has a stable operation identity.

ownership.scope: Tests, queue-state design, and review practice
ownership.boundary_text: The organization adopted the review checklist; Miguel did not own all on-call process policy.
ownership.owned_by: Miguel for technical changes; backend group for process

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question asks what changed after the incident
disclosure.allowed_summary: Replay test, reconciliation state, and review checklist
prohibited_expansion: Do not claim the change guarantees no future incidents.

relations.reason: It is the durable consequence of the incident.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Useful consequence evidence; stop after the mechanism is clear.

evidence_units.label: Unowned cluster and network operations

statement.text: The platform team owned Kubernetes upgrades, network policy, cluster capacity, and secret rotation; Miguel consumed those interfaces and raised service requirements but did not operate them.

ownership.scope: Cluster, network policy, capacity, and secrets operations
ownership.boundary_text: Miguel's service ownership did not include platform operations.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question asks about the platform or deployment boundary
disclosure.allowed_summary: Platform-owned operations and Miguel's service interface
prohibited_expansion: Do not turn this boundary into an infrastructure trivia exam.

relations.reason: Service correctness and platform operations are distinct scopes.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Should be recorded and moved past if the role does not require cluster operation.

evidence_units.label: Protected provider and customer details

statement.text: Miguel cannot disclose exact payment-provider retry windows, customer identifiers, or internal fraud thresholds; he can describe generic state transitions, failure classes, and safeguards.

ownership.boundary_text: Generic correctness reasoning remains available without proprietary details.

prohibited_reveal_conditions: Any request for exact provider timings, customer IDs, or fraud thresholds.
disclosure.reveal_trigger: Candidate states a confidentiality boundary
disclosure.allowed_summary: Generic retry and reconciliation behavior
prohibited_expansion: Never disclose exact values or identities.

relations.reason: The protected details surround the incident context.

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Refusal is appropriate and should not lower the technical assessment.

statement.text: Miguel informally reviews onboarding pull requests twice a week and prefers written examples over live whiteboard explanations.

ownership.boundary_text: This is not formal people management.

disclosure.reveal_trigger: Question about collaboration or routine
disclosure.allowed_summary: Informal onboarding review habit

evidence_units.evaluator_note: Neutral human detail that keeps the world from being only incident facts.

attribution_rules.text: Use each evidence unit's ownership status, scope, boundary, and owner exactly; paraphrase cannot widen it.
Distinguish true, qualified, protected, unavailable, unknown, and superseded evidence rather than collapsing them into a verdict.
Apply explicit correction and supersession relationships before interpreting a contradiction; a candid correction is not automatically deception.
When the frozen world marks an area protected, unowned, untested, or missed because of interviewer behavior, preserve that distinction in the evidence profile.

families.label: One-time ownership reset
families.when_legal: The resume claim is broader than the candidate's stated personal scope and the boundary has not yet been made explicit.
families.value_tradeoff: High fairness value once; little value after a truthful boundary is recorded.
acceptable_variants: Ask which design section was personal.
Ask what the candidate implemented versus reviewed.
Ask who made the final decomposition decision.

families.label: Test meaningful adjacent ownership
families.when_legal: A concrete owned subsystem is named after the broader claim is corrected.
families.value_tradeoff: High backend signal; should not be framed as consolation or expanded into the whole platform.
acceptable_variants: Probe operation identity and retries.
Probe tenant-context isolation.
Ask for a concrete artifact or negative test.

families.label: Falsifiable failure scenario
families.when_legal: A mechanism has been established and the interviewer wants to see whether it survives a changed condition.
families.value_tradeoff: High discriminative value if bounded; can become a trivia contest if it asks for unowned internals.
acceptable_variants: Change timeout ordering.
Ask what state is persisted before and after an ambiguous response.
Ask what would make reconciliation unsafe.

families.label: Incident consequence and tradeoff
families.when_legal: A production failure or subsystem is clear but the improvement's operational effect is not.
families.value_tradeoff: Tests learning and judgment without requiring a second unrelated architecture tour.
acceptable_variants: Ask what changed in tests.
Ask what new failure mode the fix accepted.
Ask how the team detects unresolved state.

families.label: Record an unowned area
families.when_legal: The candidate has explicitly named platform or proprietary boundaries.
families.value_tradeoff: Protects fairness and time; leaves an honest unknown when the role does not require that layer.
acceptable_variants: Mark cluster operations untested.
Ask only about service/platform interface.
Rotate to an owned backend surface.

families.label: Rotate to independent backend evidence
families.when_legal: The current surface is sufficiently understood or another dimension has more expected value.
families.value_tradeoff: Protects breadth; may leave some depth uncertainty that should be named.
acceptable_variants: Move from retries to isolation.
Move from incident to design tradeoff.
Close with a scoped uncertainty.

junctions.state: The resume wording is too broad, but Miguel has acknowledged team design and named a potential owned reliability slice.
tradeoffs: One scope reset is needed for fairness; repeating it has low value.
Testing the idempotency slice can recover meaningful backend signal.
Rotation is reasonable if other dimensions are more uncertain.
junctions.not_gold_note: The world does not require the reviewer to pursue idempotency specifically; tenant isolation or incident learning can also be legitimate.

junctions.state: The incident mechanism and operation-identity fix are clear, while tenant isolation remains untested.
tradeoffs: A counterfactual can test whether the design generalizes.
A second incident question risks overfitting to one failure.
Tenant coverage may offer more independent signal.
junctions.not_gold_note: More than one sensible move exists after a strong incident answer.

junctions.state: Miguel clearly states platform ownership for Kubernetes, network policy, and secrets while the target role emphasizes backend services.
tradeoffs: Recording the boundary preserves scope accuracy.
A conceptual interface question may be fair if operations matter for the role.
Endless infrastructure trivia would substitute a different role.
junctions.not_gold_note: The candidate's honest gap must remain distinct from a demonstrated weakness.

invalid_reality_violations.action: Ask whether Miguel was the architect after he has explicitly corrected the team boundary.
invalid_reality_violations.why_invalid: It adds no new ownership evidence and makes the candidate defend wording instead of demonstrating backend skill.
invalid_reality_violations.candidate_harm: Turns a resume compression into an endless character trial.

invalid_reality_violations.action: Treat idempotency or tenant isolation ownership as ownership of the entire architecture.
invalid_reality_violations.why_invalid: The facts explicitly separate a subsystem from team decomposition.
invalid_reality_violations.candidate_harm: Either inflates the candidate unfairly or later punishes him for an interviewer-created claim.

invalid_reality_violations.action: Demand exact provider timeout, fraud, or customer identifiers to validate the incident.
invalid_reality_violations.why_invalid: The details are protected and generic state reasoning is available.
invalid_reality_violations.candidate_harm: Rewards confidentiality violations and mislabels refusal as evasiveness.

invalid_reality_violations.action: Run a Kubernetes or network-policy trivia exam after the candidate states the platform boundary.
invalid_reality_violations.why_invalid: The world does not give him ownership or memory of those internals, and the target role is service-focused.
invalid_reality_violations.candidate_harm: Converts an unowned area into a false backend weakness.

invalid_reality_violations.action: Require a yes/no exactly-once guarantee without allowing a distinction between local state and external side effects.
invalid_reality_violations.why_invalid: The relevant engineering truth is conditional idempotency plus reconciliation, not a slogan.
invalid_reality_violations.candidate_harm: Penalizes precise systems reasoning for refusing an impossible guarantee.

sufficiency_conditions.minimum_turn_shape: A good interview should establish the architecture boundary once, then obtain one owned correctness mechanism, one incident or counterfactual, and a scoped read on tenant isolation or another independent dimension.

conditions.label: Architecture scope is calibrated

conditions.not_satisfied_when: The report repeats the resume word as either full truth or proof of dishonesty.

conditions.label: Retry correctness is evidenced

conditions.not_satisfied_when: The report relies on terms such as exactly once without a state mechanism.

conditions.label: Incident learning is evidenced

conditions.not_satisfied_when: The incident is reduced to blame or outcome percentage.

conditions.label: Isolation is independently assessed
